title: transfinite-cell-complex
description: A regular CW-complex-style structure whose cell set is indexed by a countable ordinal up to omega_1, with every cell of finite dimension; the transfinite content lives in the cardinality and indexing of the cell set, and the complex is the directed colimit of its finite sub-complexes. It is the cellular base needed for the aperiodic regime of the bitopological settling site, generated by generalizing the Anderson-Putnam direct-limit template from inverse-limit tiling spaces to directed-colimit cell complexes.

cells.description: the cell set cells(X), indexed by some countable initial ordinal alpha <= omega_1

indexingOrdinal.description: a countable initial ordinal alpha <= omega_1 indexing the cells

dim.description: the dimension function dim: cells(X) -> omega assigning each cell a finite (or countable) dimension

faceIncidence.description: the face-incidence relation sigma < tau on cells, holding when sigma is a face of tau, with dim sigma < dim tau

directColimitOfFiniteSubcomplexes.description: X = colim over finite F of cells(X) of X|_F: the finite-cell sub-complexes form a directed system under inclusion and X is their colimit, with no limit-cell structure at limit ordinals beyond the union of preceding cells

transfiniteSkeleta.description: for each beta <= alpha the beta-skeleton X^(beta) is the sub-complex on cells indexed by ordinals < beta; successor steps adjoin one cell, limit steps take the colimit of preceding skeleta
